title: He Called Himself Alpha and Omega… But You Missed Why That Changes Everything
paragraphs: He Called Himself Alpha and Omega… But You Missed Why That Changes Everything
There are names people give themselves to impress… and then there are names that split history in two.

Jesus didn’t introduce Himself like a philosopher trying to be understood. He didn’t soften His words to be acceptable. He said something so absolute, so eternal, that it either demands surrender… or exposes resistance.
“I am the Alpha and the Omega.”
Not a metaphor. Not a poetic exaggeration.
A claim that shakes heaven, confronts hell, and reaches into the hidden corners of your life where you still think your story is unfinished, broken, or too far gone.
In the Greek text of Revelation, it is written:

“Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ”
(Egō eimi to Alpha kai to Ō)
“I am the Alpha and the Omega.”

Alpha — the first letter.
Omega — the last.

The beginning.
The end.
But if you read that too quickly, you will miss the weight of what He was really saying.
Because this wasn’t just about time.
It was about authority over everything in between.
Before your first mistake… He already was.
After your worst failure… He still is.
And right now, in the middle of your confusion, your guilt, your questions, your silent battles — He hasn’t stepped back.
He is still writing.
The Hebrew mind would have heard something deeper. In Isaiah, God declares:

“אֲנִי רִאשׁוֹן וַאֲנִי אַחֲרוֹן”
(Ani rishon va’ani acharon)
“I am the first and I am the last.” (Isaiah 44:6)
This is not just a title.
This is identity.
This is God Himself speaking.
So when Jesus stands in Revelation and says, “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” He is not borrowing language.
He is revealing who He truly is.
Not a teacher trying to guide you.
Not just a Savior trying to rescue you.
But God in flesh… stepping into your timeline… rewriting what sin tried to destroy.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because if He is truly the Alpha and the Omega… then He is not just the author of your life.
He is also the rightful editor.
Meaning some things in your story… have to be removed.
Some habits… rewritten.
Some identities… deleted.
Some sins… confronted.
And we don’t like that part.
We love the idea that Jesus finishes our story.
We struggle with the truth that He also has the authority to change it.

In Aramaic, the language closest to Jesus’ spoken words, the weight of identity is not just in titles but in presence. When Jesus said “I am” — “ܐܢܐ ܐܢܐ” (Ana Ana) — it echoed the divine name revealed to Moses.
“I AM WHO I AM.”

Not “I was.”
Not “I will be.”
But present. Active. Unchanging.
So when He says Alpha and Omega, He is not describing a timeline.
He is declaring that every moment in your life is under His sovereign gaze.
The beginning you regret.
The middle you’re struggling through.
The ending you’re afraid of.
He holds it all.
Which means your scandal… is not your final chapter.
Your shame… is not your identity.
Your failure… is not your ending.
Because Jesus does not enter stories to observe them.
He enters them to rewrite them.
That’s why the cross makes no sense to a casual reader.
Because the Alpha… allowed Himself to be treated like He was nothing.
The Beginning… stepped into broken humanity.
The Eternal One… took on time, pain, betrayal, abandonment.
Why?
So that your ending wouldn’t be separation… but redemption.
“Τετέλεσται” (Tetelestai)
“It is finished.”
Not finished like defeat.
Finished like a debt fully paid.
Finished like a story redirected.
Finished like grace breaking into a life that thought it was beyond saving.
And maybe that’s you.
You’ve been telling yourself this is just who you are now.
This is just how your life turned out.
This is just the consequences you have to carry forever.
But if Jesus is truly the Alpha and the Omega…
Then your story doesn’t belong to your past.
It belongs to Him.
And He is not done.
Be honest… this hit something you’ve been avoiding.
And if this stirred something deeper in you… don’t stay at the surface.
Because real discipleship doesn’t happen in occasional moments… it happens in daily surrender.
If you truly want to glorify God… then don’t just feel convicted.
Support what is feeding your spirit.
Help spread truth in a world starving for it.
Because the truth is…
The enemy is hoping you forget who is holding your story.
But Jesus is still writing… and He never leaves a story unfinished.
And here’s the part that will stay with you long after you leave this page:
The One who wrote your beginning… is still standing at your ending… waiting to meet you there with grace.
